comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom develops complex digital/mixed signal CMOS and analog III-V semiconductor devices, offering thousands of products for markets including AI networking, data centers, telecommunications, and factory automation.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and Broadcom both characterize their businesses as developing specialized semiconductor devices and products for specific high-performance markets, including AI and data centers. AMD claims to be a 'leader in embedded computing' delivering 'high-performance and scalability' in 'AI processing capabilities' for automotive, industrial, and data centers. Broadcom similarly states it develops 'semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal... devices' used in 'AI networking and connectivity' and 'data center servers,' differentiating through 'high-performance design and integration capabilities.' Both disclose a product-centric strategy focused on specialized silicon for these demanding applications.

sentences.text: We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.
We also incorporate dedicated AI processing capabilities into our embedded portfolio.
We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor ("CMOS") based devices and analog III-V based products.

We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes ("STB"), broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.

We differentiate ourselves through our high-performance design and integration capabilities and focus on developing semiconductor products for target markets where we believe we can earn attractive margins.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and Intel both disclose broadening their product portfolios beyond traditional CPUs to include specialized accelerators and heterogeneous computing devices. AMD highlights its 'full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs' that incorporate AI capabilities. Similarly, Intel states it delivers 'a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators' to meet diverse computing needs, with a strategy to 'develop and offer leading products across each of these architectural categories.' Both companies emphasize a multi-architecture approach to address varied workloads.

As part of our strategy, we seek to develop and offer leading products across each of these architectural categories.
